problem: The R3-3 fix turned the EISDIR from sha256OfFile into a typed NotARegularFileError, and all three manifest callers now catch it. The other caller of the shared helper does not: shaDriftedSinceInstall, called from doctorIntegration at installer.ts:698. When a recorded install-state sha256 key names a directory, it throws out of doctorIntegration. plan.ts:519 is also unguarded, but it is only reachable through a literal manifest path that is a directory, and the bundled manifest has none.
impact: `keryx integrations doctor --runtime all` exits 1 with the one-line error and prints no report for any runtime. This is the same abort-all class that installer.ts's own 'review round 3, M3' comment fixed for invalid settings JSON. It predates this PR (bff0a030 throws a raw EISDIR in the same place), so it is not a regression. The typed error now makes the fix trivial.
suggested_fix: In shaDriftedSinceInstall, catch NotARegularFileError and return true, so the surface is reported as drift like any other live-vs-recorded mismatch. Optionally, have resolveGlob in glob.ts return a literal path only when it is a regular file, so plan.ts cannot reach the throw. Add an installer.test.ts case in which a sha256 key names a directory and doctor must return a report.
evidence: scratchpad/r4/integ.ts at HEAD: 'doctor THREW NotARegularFileError "adir" exists but is not a regular file'. The same repro gives 'install OK' and 'uninstall OK'. On the pre-fix tree (scratchpad/r4/pre, bff0a030): 'doctor THREW Error EISDIR'. CLI: `keryx integrations doctor --runtime all` → the error message, exit=1.

sites: src/integrations/install-state.ts:223 (not reachable: hashPaths is always the surface's settings file)

problem: R3-4's new `unreadable` diagnostics appear only in `skills stocktake --json`. The human stocktake output never mentions that a skill was skipped. `loadSkillCatalog`, which eval and scout use, drops the diagnostics altogether, so `skills eval project-skills/bad --scope all` on an EACCES skill says 'unknown skill id: project-skills/bad' rather than naming the read error.
impact: A project skill disappears silently from a human-readable stocktake, and eval misreports an existing but unreadable skill as nonexistent. Nothing crashes any more; this is a diagnostic gap only.
suggested_fix: Print an 'Unreadable: N (path: code)' line in the human stocktake output when report.unreadable is non-empty. In eval and scout, use loadSkillCatalogWithDiagnostics, and when the requested id matches an unreadable path, give the errno instead of 'unknown skill id'.
evidence: Fixture scratchpad/r4/stk with a chmod 000 project-skills/bad/SKILL.md. `--json` gives unreadable [{code: EACCES}]. The human output is 'Stocktake (all): 75 skill(s) … Cache: …' with no mention of 'bad'. `skills eval project-skills/bad --scope all` gives 'unknown skill id: project-skills/bad'.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every consumer of loadSkillCatalog and loadSkillCatalogWithDiagnostics reached from the three `--scope all` verbs
